summary: If coins are found on the floor between two collection boxes, they go to the closer box. If they are right in the middle, they go to the box with the stricter rule.

chunks.en: Coins found between the shekalim box and the gift box:
chunks.st: If money was found on the floor of the Temple between one of the collection horns marked shekels and the collection horn marked free-will offerings, that is to say,
chunks.stMore: between the first and the thirteenth collection horns, in which funds contributed to the Temple were stored, the following distinctions apply:

chunks.en: if closer to the shekalim, they go to the shekalim;
chunks.st: If the money was found closer to the horn marked shekels, it is allocated to the shekels;

chunks.en: if closer to the gift box, they go to the gift box;
chunks.st: if it was found closer to the horn marked free-will offerings, it is allocated to free-will offerings;

chunks.en: if right in the middle, they go to the gift box.
chunks.st: and if it was equidistant from the horn marked shekels and the horn marked free-will offerings, it is allocated to free-will offerings.

chunks.en: Between the wood box and the levonah box:
chunks.st: If the money was found between the horn marked wood and the horn marked frankincense, that is, between the fifth and sixth horns,

chunks.en: if closer to the wood, they go to the wood;
chunks.st: if it was closer to the horn marked wood, it is allocated to wood;

chunks.en: if closer to the levonah, they go to the levonah;
chunks.st: if it was closer to the horn marked frankincense, it is allocated to frankincense;

chunks.en: if right in the middle, they go to the levonah.
chunks.st: and if it was found equidistant from both, it is allocated to frankincense.

chunks.en: Between the bird pairs box and the young birds for an olah box:
chunks.st: If the money was found between the horn marked pairs of bird-offerings and the horn marked doves for burnt-offerings, i.e., between the third and the fourth horns,

chunks.en: if closer to the bird pairs, they go to the bird pairs;
chunks.st: if it is closer to the horn marked pairs of bird-offerings, it is allocated to pairs of bird-offerings;

chunks.en: if closer to the young birds for an olah, they go there;
chunks.st: if it was found closer to the horn marked doves for burnt-offerings, it is allocated to doves for burnt-offerings;

chunks.en: if right in the middle, they go to the young birds for an olah.
chunks.st: and if it was found equidistant from both, it is allocated to doves for burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: Between plain money and maaser sheni money:
chunks.st: And similarly, if money was found anywhere else between a container for ordinary, non-sacred money and one containing second-tithe money, the following distinctions apply:

chunks.en: if closer to the plain money, it is plain money;
chunks.st: If the money was found closer to the non-sacred money, it is allocated to the non-sacred money;

chunks.en: if closer to maaser sheni, it is maaser sheni;
chunks.st: if it was found closer to second-tithe money, it is allocated to second-tithe money;

chunks.en: if right in the middle, it is maaser sheni.
chunks.st: and if it was found equidistant from both, it is allocated to second-tithe money.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: we follow what is closer, even to be lenient,
chunks.st: In cases of doubt, the ruling follows whichever is closer, even if this involves being lenient,

chunks.en: and if right in the middle, we are strict.
chunks.st: but if the money was found equidistant from both, the ruling follows whichever allocation involves being stringent.

summary: When we find coins and don't know whose they are, we decide by where and when they were found. Near the animal sellers, or in Yerushalayim on Yom Tov, they are counted as maaser sheni money.
stIntro: This mishna considers other situations in which something is found and its source is unknown.

chunks.en: Coins found near the animal sellers
chunks.explain: In Yerushalayim, people bought animals with maaser sheni money.
chunks.st: Money found before animal merchants in Jerusalem

chunks.en: are always maaser sheni.
chunks.st: is always presumed to be second-tithe money.
chunks.stMore: The presumption is based on the fact that in Jerusalem, most of the animals are bought with second-tithe money and sacrificed as peace-offerings.

chunks.en: On Har HaBayis, they are plain money.
chunks.st: And money found on the Temple Mount is presumed to be non-sacred money.

chunks.en: In Yerushalayim at the time of Yom Tov, they are maaser sheni,
chunks.st: And with regard to money found in the rest of Jerusalem, the following distinction applies:

chunks.en: and the rest of the year, they are plain money.
chunks.st: If it was found during the rest of the days of the year, it is presumed to be non-sacred money, but if it was found during the time of a pilgrim Festival, it is all presumed to be second-tithe money,
chunks.stMore: because most of the money found in Jerusalem at the time of a Festival is second-tithe money.

summary: If meat is found in the Azarah or in Yerushalayim, we decide what kind of korban it probably is, and it must be burned. Meat found outside Yerushalayim may sometimes be eaten.

chunks.en: Meat that was found in the Azarah:
chunks.st: The mishna continues: With regard to meat that was found in the Temple courtyard,
chunks.stMore: and it is not known from whence it came, the halakha is as follows:

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: whole parts are olah korbanos,
chunks.st: If it is whole limbs of the animal, in the manner that burnt-offerings are brought to the altar, it is presumed to be burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: and small pieces are chataos.
chunks.st: And if it is in small pieces, it is presumed to be sin-offerings.

chunks.en: In Yerushalayim, it is shelamim.
chunks.st: And if the meat, in whatever form, is found in the city of Jerusalem, as opposed to the courtyard, it is presumed to be the meat of peace-offerings,
chunks.stMore: as most of the meat in Jerusalem is the meat of peace-offerings.

chunks.en: Either way, it is left until it spoils
chunks.explain: Maybe its time to be eaten has passed already.
chunks.st: Since it is possible that the time during which it is permitted to eat any of it has already passed, both this and that, whether it is determined to be the meat of burnt-offerings or the meat of peace-offerings, its form must be allowed to decay, i.e., it must be left until it is definitely disqualified,

chunks.en: and it is taken out to the place for burning.
chunks.st: and then it must be taken out to the place of burning, where offerings that have become disqualified are burned.

chunks.en: If it was found outside Yerushalayim:
chunks.st: With regard to meat found in the outlying areas, outside of Jerusalem,

chunks.en: whole parts are neveilos, not kosher,
chunks.st: if it is in the form of whole limbs, the meat presumably comes from carcasses
chunks.stMore: of animals that were not properly slaughtered, for meat unfit for eating was generally cut up into full limbs, to be fed to dogs or sold to gentiles.

words.note: Animals that died without shechitah, which may not be eaten.

chunks.en: and small pieces are allowed.
chunks.st: But if it is in small pieces, it is presumably kosher and permitted to be eaten,
chunks.stMore: as kosher meat was ordinarily cut up into small pieces.

chunks.en: And at Yom Tov time, when there is lots of meat,
chunks.st: And if meat is found at the time of a Festival, when meat is plentiful, so that it is generally not cut up into small pieces,

chunks.en: even whole parts are allowed.
chunks.st: then even whole limbs are permitted to be eaten.

summary: An animal found near Yerushalayim is probably a korban. Males are counted as olah korbanos and females as shelamim, and Rabbi Yehuda adds a rule for the korban Pesach.

chunks.en: An animal that was found
chunks.st: If an animal that is fit for the altar was found straying,

chunks.en: from Yerushalayim up to Migdal Eder,
chunks.st: from Jerusalem and as far as Migdal Eder,

chunks.en: or the same distance in any direction:
chunks.st: and similarly if it was found within that distance from Jerusalem in any other direction,
chunks.stMore: it is presumed that the animal came from Jerusalem. Most of the animals in Jerusalem were designated for offerings, and presumably this one was as well.

chunks.en: males are olah korbanos,
chunks.st: Males are presumed to be burnt-offerings, as only males are brought as burnt-offerings.

chunks.en: females are shelamim.
chunks.st: Females are presumed to be peace-offerings, as it is permitted to bring a female peace-offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: One that is fit for a korban Pesach
chunks.st: An animal that is fit for the Paschal offering, i.e., a one-year-old male lamb or kid,

chunks.en: is a korban Pesach,
chunks.st: is presumed to be a Paschal offering,

chunks.en: if it is within thirty days before Pesach.
chunks.st: provided that it was found within thirty days before the Festival of Passover.

summary: At first, a person who found such an animal had to pay for its wine offerings, so people stopped taking the animals. So beis din made a rule that the community pays for them.

chunks.en: At first they would take a pledge from the one who found it,
chunks.st: Originally, the court would seize collateral from one who found such an animal,

chunks.en: until he brings its wine offerings.
chunks.st: as security until he would bring with it the libations associated with this offering,
chunks.stMore: as if the found animal were his own and he had committed himself to bring the libations.

chunks.en: Then people began to leave it and run away.
chunks.st: This brought about a situation in which those who found the animals began leaving them where they found them, and absconding, so as not to become liable for the libations.

chunks.en: Beis din made a rule
chunks.st: The court therefore instituted that the libations accompanying these offerings

chunks.en: that its wine offerings come from the money of the community.
chunks.st: would come from public funds, that is, from the Temple treasury.

summary: Beis din made seven rules about korbanos. This mishnah tells some of them: when the community pays for wine offerings, and for the mincha of a Kohen Gadol who passed away.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.en: Beis din made seven rules,
chunks.st: The court instituted seven ordinances
chunks.stMore: with regard to the financial aspects of offerings and consecrations.

chunks.en: and this is one of them.
chunks.st: And this ordinance, namely, that the cost of the libations accompanying the sacrifice of a found animal is borne by the public, is one of them.

chunks.en: A non-Jew who sent his olah from far away
chunks.st: These are the other ordinances: If a gentile sent his burnt-offering from abroad, outside Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: and sent wine offerings with it,
chunks.st: and he sent with it money for the purchase of the libations that must accompany it,

chunks.en: they are brought from his money.
chunks.st: the libations are offered at his expense.

chunks.en: And if not, they are brought from the money of the community.
chunks.st: And if the gentile did not cover the cost of the libations, it is a condition of the court that the libations are sacrificed at the public’s expense, with funds taken from the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: And also a ger who passed away and left korbanos:
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of a convert who died without heirs and left animals that he had designated as offerings.

chunks.en: if he has wine offerings,
chunks.st: If he has the libations,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if he also had set aside libations or money for that purpose,

chunks.en: they are brought from his.
chunks.st: the libations are sacrificed from his estate.

chunks.en: And if not, they are brought from the money of the community.
chunks.st: And if he did not do so, the libations are sacrificed from public funds.

chunks.en: And it is a rule of beis din
chunks.st: And another ordinance: It is a condition of the court

chunks.en: about a Kohen Gadol who passed away,
chunks.st: with regard to a High Priest who died,
chunks.stMore: and a new High Priest had not yet been appointed in his place,

chunks.en: that his mincha is brought from the money of the community.
chunks.st: that his meal-offering, i.e., the griddle-cake offering that the High Priest would bring each day from one-tenth of an ephah of flour, would be sacrificed from public funds.

words.note: The Kohen Gadol brought a flour korban every day.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: from the money of his family.
chunks.st: It was brought from the property of the High Priest’s heirs, i.e., his estate, and not from public funds.

chunks.en: And it was brought whole.
chunks.explain: All of it at once, not half in the morning and half at night.
chunks.st: In any event, the offering was not brought as it would have been brought by the High Priest himself were he still alive, half in the morning and half in the evening, but rather it was sacrificed all at once, from a whole one-tenth of an ephah.

summary: More of beis din's rules: the Kohanim may use the salt and wood, using the parah adumah's ashes is not me'ilah, and the community pays for birds that became pasul.

chunks.en: About the salt
chunks.st: The fourth ordinance was about the salt in the Temple that was designated for salting the offerings,

words.note: Salt that was put on the korbanos.

chunks.en: and about the wood,
chunks.st: and the fifth was about the wood that was used for the burning of the offerings.

chunks.en: that the Kohanim may use them,
chunks.explain: To cook the meat of the korbanos they eat.
chunks.st: These ordinances decreed that the priests may use them also to prepare the meat of the offerings that they eat.

chunks.he: וְעַל הַפָּרָה שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מוֹעֲלִין בְּאֶפְרָהּ,
chunks.en: and about the parah adumah, that using its ashes is not me'ilah,
chunks.st: And the sixth ordinance concerned the red heifer: that deriving benefit from its ashes is not considered misusing consecrated property.

chunks.en: and about bird pairs that became pasul,
chunks.st: And the seventh ordinance was about disqualified pairs of bird-offerings:

words.note: Not good to be brought as a korban.

chunks.en: that new ones come from the money of the community.
chunks.st: It ruled that their replacements should come from public funds.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei disagreed and says:

chunks.en: The one who supplies the bird pairs
chunks.st: The expense does not fall upon the public, but rather upon whoever supplies all the pairs of bird-offerings to the Temple;

chunks.en: supplies the ones that became pasul.
chunks.st: he must also supply, at no additional charge, the replacements for the disqualified birds.
